existing_architecture.summary: Two independent simulation stacks share the same LIF neuron, spike recorder, statistics helpers and observation layer. The FAFB stack (BrainSimulator + SynapseModel) derives signs from a graph vocabulary. The BANC stack (BancSimulator + BancSignedSynapses) uses an explicit BancSynapsePolicy built from published annotations and a declared weight transform. Neither stack has a reward input, a mutable effective-weight layer, a checkpoint of learned state, or any train/evaluation split. FAFB and BANC identities are never merged and Phase 4H.4 established that the tested BANC sensory-to-motor pathway produced no motor spikes.

stacks.weights: derived at construction from integer edge weights and the configured power or linear transform
stacks.role_in_phase_5: must remain unchanged and behaviourally frozen; not the target of Phase 5 learning

stacks.role_in_phase_5: the structural substrate and the default fixed-weight reference condition

order: synapses.advance(): decay existing currents and deliver the delayed spike packet
current = noise + background + synaptic current + stimulation current
input_schedule.apply(step, step * dt_ms, current) adds scheduled current in place
spikes = neurons.step(current): returns the indices of neurons that fired at this step
synapses.propagate(spikes): routes spikes through outgoing edges into the delay buffer
step_loop.consequence_for_plasticity: At each loop boundary both the presynaptic spikes (argument to propagate) and the postsynaptic spikes (returned by neurons.step) are available, but propagate currently returns only a transmission count, not the edge indices. Per-edge credit assignment requires the edge index vector that propagate already computes internally at brain/banc_simulator.py:199-205.

interfaces.name: input schedule
interfaces.contract: apply(step: int, time_ms: float, current_pa: np.ndarray) -> None, mutating current in place; exposed stimulated_indices
interfaces.plasticity_relevance: reusable as an input driver, but not as a reward source and not as evidence of a biological pathway

interfaces.name: neuron step
interfaces.contract: LIFPopulation.step(current_pa) -> np.ndarray[int] of spiking neuron indices
interfaces.plasticity_relevance: supplies both pre- and post-synaptic spike sets at zero API change

interfaces.plasticity_relevance: insufficient as-is for per-edge eligibility; needs edge-index attribution

interfaces.plasticity_relevance: read-only outcome measurement; must not be the reward source in the primary task

interfaces.name: decoder
interfaces.plasticity_relevance: left/right/jump are decoder labels, not identified biological commands; useful as a diagnostic only

weight_lifecycle: BancConnectome stores integer edge synapse counts (edge_weight, int32) plus CSR indices; it is built once and loaded read-only.

build_synapse_policy(graph, node_table, sign_policy, weight_policy) at brain/banc_synapse_policy.py:354 produces float32 edge_exc_weight and edge_inh_weight. Sign is chosen from verified annotations only in the primary policy; unknown-sign edges carry zero.

BancSignedSynapses.__init__ assigns self.edge_exc_weight = policy.edge_exc_weight (brain/banc_simulator.py:107-108). The docstring at lines 77-78 states the arrays are shared with the policy, not copied.
propagate reads those arrays but never writes them. The arrays are immutable by convention only; there is no write protection and no API boundary.
No layer exists for learned weights. Any in-place update of the current arrays would silently corrupt the policy object and every later run that reuses it.
determinism: Each run constructs a fresh np.random.default_rng(seed) at brain/banc_simulator.py:404. There is no global RNG use in the simulator loop.
Spike times are recorded as float32 at (step + 1) * dt_ms by SpikeRecorder.record (brain/neural_activity.py:59).
Phase 4H records spike_hash and decision_hash for every condition. A plasticity implementation that changes RNG draw order or float accumulation order will change these hashes even with no learning.
Weight order is fixed by the CSR edge ordering; any update vector must follow the same ordering to remain reproducible.

design_principles: The fixed-weight simulator remains the default and the reference; plasticity is opt-in and lives outside brain/ wherever possible.
Structural synapse counts and initial transformed weights are immutable read-only artifacts. Learned weight is a separate additive or multiplicative layer.
No default simulation behaviour changes. With learning rate zero, the plastic pathway must reproduce the fixed-weight pathway bit-for-bit.
Reward is a computational scalar from an external task. It is not dopamine, not a neuromodulator measurement and not a biological reinforcement signal.
Eligibility traces are a model of short-lived synaptic tagging. They are not measured synaptic states.
Sign is preserved by construction. A structural excitatory edge never becomes inhibitory and vice versa. This avoids inventing biological sign changes from a computational rule.
Only edges with a verified sign in the primary policy are plastic. Unknown-sign edges carry zero and stay zero.
Training and evaluation are separated by seed and, where possible, by task instance. No evaluation seed is used for any update.
Every run records enough state to reproduce it: config digest, dataset digest, policy digest, initial weight digest, RNG streams and final weight digest.

weight, trace, saturation and timing diagnostics; JSON-serialisable

declared a priori parameters by section; no value may be tuned on evaluation results
per-step runners, logging, pre-registration, stored results, analysis and plots
reward representation, predictor, RPE and logging tests
trace accumulation, decay, reset, sparse consistency and benchmark tests

task, split, control and leakage tests

layers.structural_count: int32 edge-level synapse count from BancConnectome.edge_weight; read-only
layers.structural_pa: float32 transformed weight from BancSynapsePolicy.edge_exc_weight / edge_inh_weight; read-only
layers.initial_pa: float32 copy of structural_pa at the start of a run, used for bounds and for reporting drift; read-only
layers.learned_delta_pa: float32 signed additive change owned by the plasticity layer
layers.effective_pa: float32 structural_pa + learned_delta_pa, clipped to declared bounds and to the sign class

invariants: structural_count, structural_pa and initial_pa are never written after construction
learned_delta_pa is zero for every edge excluded by the sign policy
effective_pa is never negative for an excitatory edge and never positive for an inhibitory edge
effective_pa stays within [lower_factor * initial_pa, upper_factor * initial_pa] for each edge with a nonzero initial weight
structural_pa + learned_delta_pa equals effective_pa before clipping; clipping is reported, not hidden
the sum and maximum absolute update are recorded every step

bounds.status: declared a priori; not fitted to any outcome
bounds.rationale: a bounded multiplicative range keeps the assumed current regime and prevents runaway excitation, while allowing measurable change. It is a modelling choice, not a physiological boundary.

sign_preservation.mechanism: store a per-edge sign class (+1 exc, -1 inh, 0 excluded); after every update, clamp delta so that sign * effective_pa >= 0 and, for nonzero initial weights, stays within the relative bounds
sign_preservation.sign_flip_count: must be reported and must be exactly zero

eligibility_traces.state: one float32 value per plastic edge, held in a contiguous array indexed by the same CSR edge index used by propagate
eligibility_traces.decay: e_ij(t) = lambda * e_ij(t-1), lambda = exp(-dt_ms / tau_e_ms), with a default tau_e_ms declared in configs/plasticity.yaml
eligibility_traces.accumulation: e_ij(t) += f(pre_i(t), post_j(t)) on edges whose presynaptic neuron fired at step t and whose postsynaptic neuron fired at the same step or within the declared coincidence window
eligibility_traces.coincidence_convention: the simulator delivers a presynaptic spike to the postsynaptic neuron after the configured delay. The trace pairing convention must be declared explicitly (same-step coincidence versus delay-matched coincidence) and tested on a two-neuron hand-computed case. The default recommendation is delay-matched: a presynaptic spike at step t is paired with postsynaptic spikes observed at the step at which the packet is delivered.
fallbacks: pre-only trace: per-neuron trace, cheaper, but does not encode coincidence
pre-post with a post baseline: subtract a running post rate to avoid saturation
eligibility_traces.storage: dense per-edge float32 is 1,535,710 * 4 = 6,142,840 bytes (about 5.86 MiB) for the threshold-5 graph; per-neuron traces are negligible
cost_control: lazy decay: store a last-update step per active edge or use a global decay reference plus per-edge timestamps, so a step with no spikes touches only active edges
apply reward-driven updates only at reward events, not every simulation step
measure both dense and sparse strategies in 5C before choosing the default

reward.type: computational scalar supplied by an external task or script; never a biological neuromodulator measurement

representation.timing: immediate or delayed; the delay is declared and logged
representation.validation: finite, bounded, unit-documented; a per-run reward stream digest is recorded

reward.primary_signal: task outcome independent of MotorDecoder labels; for example a synthetic target reached or not reached in a controlled task

predictor.role: separate module that estimates V(s); it is not part of the synaptic rule
predictor.configuration: gamma, state representation and value-update rule are declared a priori
predictor.warning: the temporal-difference formulation is one model of reward prediction, not the only biologically plausible one

prohibited_sources: MotorDecoder LEFT/RIGHT/JUMP output as the primary reward, because that is circular
any biological dopamine, octopamine or serotonin measurement, which is not available
Phase 4H sensory event labels presented as verified reward predictors

update_rule.form: Delta_w_ij = eta * delta_t * e_ij(t), applied to learned_delta_pa and then bounded and sign-clipped
update_rule.modularity: the rule consumes an eligibility value and a prediction error; it does not hardcode reward polarity or synaptic sign, and it does not import the motor decoder
update_rule.cadence: configurable; the recommended default applies reward-driven updates at reward events using the accumulated prediction error, which keeps the per-step cost off the full edge set
parameters: eta: configurable learning rate, declared a priori
minimum_pa and maximum_pa: absolute weight bounds
lower_factor and upper_factor: relative bounds around the initial weight
delta_clip: absolute bound on one reward-driven update
post_baseline_tau_ms: optional post-rate baseline for the coincidence term
update_rule.numerical_safety: reject non-finite reward, prediction, trace or weight; clip every update; record clamp hits; abort on non-finite state
update_rule.sign_preservation: baseline magnitude plasticity retains the configured excitatory or inhibitory sign; sign plasticity is excluded unless a separately justified experiment investigates it
update_rule.zero_reward_behaviour: zero reward must produce zero update when the prediction error is zero; this is tested explicitly
update_rule.zero_learning_contract: eta = 0 must produce effective weights identical to structural weights and a spike hash identical to the fixed-weight reference for the same seed and inputs
update_rule.not_claimed: a nonzero update is not evidence of learning; only held-out task improvement over matched controls can support that claim

integration_mode.recommended: separate PlasticSimulator loop in plasticity/plastic_simulator.py that mirrors brain/banc_simulator.py:440-483 and composes LIFPopulation, SpikeRecorder, PlasticSignedSynapses and PlasticityEngine
integration_mode.why_not_patch_core_first: the fixed-weight loop is a validated artifact with golden spike hashes; duplicating the loop in a new package keeps brain/ untouched and makes equivalence testable
integration_mode.future_option: if duplication becomes a maintenance risk, add a keyword-only optional hook to BancSimulator with None default and a bit-identical regression test. This is not part of 5A and must be approved separately.
integration_mode.no_change_guarantee: Phase 5A modifies no source file; Phases 5B-5D must not modify brain/, motor/ or sensory/ without explicit approval

contents: eligibility traces when the checkpoint requires them
random seed and RNG stream states
initial weight digest, structural graph checksum and policy digest
explicit statement that learned weights are model outputs
checkpointing.refusal_policy: load fails if any digest or checksum differs; saved learning state must be verified to belong to the correct graph; no silent partial load

diagnostics.abort_criteria: declared before running: non-finite weight or trace, any sign flip, membrane or current non-finite, or firing rate above a declared ceiling

determinism.rng: plasticity uses its own np.random.Generator constructed from a SeedSequence child derived from the run seed; it never draws from the simulator RNG
determinism.order: edge updates follow CSR edge order; reductions are single-threaded and stable
determinism.tests: same seed twice must give identical weight digest and spike hash; changing an unrelated stream must not change the others

memory_and_cost_estimates.dense_trace: about 5.86 MiB per per-edge float32 array
memory_and_cost_estimates.weight_layers: four float32 arrays over all edges are about 23.4 MiB; over signed edges only about 10.4 MiB
memory_and_cost_estimates.dense_decay_per_run: a 300 ms run at dt 0.5 ms has 600 steps; decaying 1,535,710 edges every step is about 921 million element updates per run, so lazy or sparse decay is the recommended default
memory_and_cost_estimates.status: estimates only; 5C must benchmark trace storage and decay, and 5D must measure wall time and peak memory of a full plastic run before the design is frozen

experimental_strategy.substrate: controlled synthetic inputs and outputs; the unproven Phase 4H sensory-to-motor pathway is not used as evidence and is not required
experimental_strategy.dataset_separation: FAFB and BANC remain separate; no BANC data is forced into the FAFB simulator without a validated adapter
experimental_strategy.primary_task: one task chosen from input-to-action association, delayed-reward association, a two-choice task or a simple sequential decision task, with a written justification before any run
conditions_5e: B plastic network with reward modulation
C plastic network with zero reward
D plastic network with shuffled rewards
E plastic network with randomized connectivity
F plastic network with disabled eligibility traces
G an appropriate non-biological learning baseline if feasible; otherwise document the exclusion
design: no training performance reported as generalisation
identical task conditions across comparable groups
experimental_strategy.failure_policy: if learning does not occur, report the negative result; success criteria are not changed after seeing results
comparison_5f: a conventional learning baseline where it can be implemented fairly
experimental_strategy.interpretation: separate structural facts, annotation-derived assumptions, computational approximations, measured outcomes and hypotheses; computational weight updates are not biological synaptic plasticity

scientific_assumptions.assumption: The existing LIF neuron parameters and exponential synapse dynamics remain valid for a plastic network.
scientific_assumptions.note: the neuron is unchanged; plasticity acts on currents, not on membrane parameters

scientific_assumptions.assumption: A scalar computational reward can stand in for a reinforcement signal.
scientific_assumptions.note: no dopamine, octopamine or serotonin physiology is modelled or measured

scientific_assumptions.assumption: A short-lived eligibility trace is a useful model of synaptic tagging.
scientific_assumptions.note: no biological time constant is claimed; tau_e is declared, not measured

scientific_assumptions.assumption: A three-factor product of eligibility and prediction error is an adequate update rule for this experiment.
scientific_assumptions.note: the rule is a construct; a successful synthetic task does not validate it biologically

scientific_assumptions.assumption: Sign preservation is the correct constraint for this model.
scientific_assumptions.note: predicted transmitters are not verified physiology; allowing sign flips would invent biological claims from an annotation prior

scientific_assumptions.assumption: The 0.5x to 2x relative weight bounds are a reasonable declared range.
scientific_assumptions.note: bounds prevent runaway excitation; they are not measured synaptic bounds

scientific_assumptions.assumption: Only verified-sign edges are plastic in the primary condition.
scientific_assumptions.note: unknown-sign edges carry zero current and remain zero; results are conditional on the verified-sign subgraph

scientific_assumptions.assumption: Synapse counts transformed by the declared weight policy are an acceptable initial weight scale.
scientific_assumptions.note: synapse count is not conductance; the learned layer is reported separately

scientific_assumptions.assumption: A synthetic task with explicit train and evaluation seeds is an appropriate first learning test.
scientific_assumptions.note: it tests the implementation, not Subway Surfers performance and not a biological pathway

scientific_assumptions.assumption: Uniform propagation delay is adequate for delay-matched eligibility pairing in the primary design.
scientific_assumptions.note: per-edge delay is not available; the uniform 1 ms delay is declared and tested explicitly

scientific_assumptions.assumption: The candidate subgraph used by the Phase 4H harness is an acceptable substrate for Phase 5 learning experiments.
scientific_assumptions.note: incoming edges at the subgraph boundary are cut; plasticity applies only to internal edges and this must be reported

scientific_assumptions.assumption: Deterministic replay is sufficient for reproducibility.
scientific_assumptions.note: determinism is not robustness; multiple seeds and held-out evaluation are still required

non_claims: No reward signal, eligibility trace or weight update is implemented in Phase 5A.
No biological dopamine, neuromodulator, receptor or plasticity mechanism is modelled.
A computational reward is not a biological reward.
A prediction error is a model variable, not a measured neural signal.
A weight change is not evidence of learning.
Synthetic-task improvement would not demonstrate Subway Surfers performance.
LEFT, RIGHT and JUMP are decoder labels, not identified biological motor commands.
Phase 4H.4 did not demonstrate a functional sensory-to-motor pathway, and Phase 5A does not reinterpret it.
FAFB and BANC are separate datasets with separate graphs; identities are never merged.
Predicted BANC neurotransmitters are not verified physiological facts.
Structural synapse counts are not conductances.
Learned weights must never be written into, or presented as, the structural connectome.
Determinism is not robustness, and a single seed is not evidence.
No claim of biological realism, biological learning or behavioural competence is made by this architecture.

integration_risks.risk: In-place learning corrupts the shared BancSynapsePolicy arrays.
integration_risks.evidence: brain/banc_simulator.py:107-108 assigns the policy arrays directly and the docstring at lines 77-78 says they are shared, not copied.
integration_risks.mitigation: copy weights into an owned effective array; mark structural, initial and policy arrays read-only with ndarray.setflags(write=False); assert SHA-256 equality before and after every run
integration_risks.test: policy digest and structural digest unchanged after training; attempting to write raises

integration_risks.evidence: Phase 4H spike hashes are the published contract for the fixed-weight condition.
integration_risks.mitigation: keep PlasticSimulator separate; eta = 0 equivalence test against BancSimulator with the same seed and inputs; no edits to brain/ in 5B-5D without approval
integration_risks.test: bit-identical spike hash, decision hash and summary counters at eta = 0

integration_risks.risk: RNG draw order changes and breaks reproducibility.
integration_risks.evidence: BancSimulator constructs a fresh default_rng(seed) at line 404 and consumes it only for noise; plasticity would add new draws if implemented carelessly.
integration_risks.mitigation: separate SeedSequence child streams for simulation, task, reward and shuffled reward; never draw from the simulator RNG; record stream states
integration_risks.test: same seed twice gives identical digests; toggling an unrelated stream leaves the simulation stream unchanged

integration_risks.risk: Dense per-step trace decay is too expensive at 1,535,710 edges.
integration_risks.evidence: 600 steps at dt 0.5 ms times 1.5 million edges is about 921 million updates per 300 ms run.
integration_risks.mitigation: lazy decay with per-edge timestamps or sparse active-edge updates; reward-driven updates only at reward events; benchmark in 5D
integration_risks.test: measured wall time and memory on the full threshold-5 graph with a declared budget

integration_risks.risk: Delay misattribution produces the wrong pre/post pairing.
integration_risks.evidence: propagate runs after neurons.step and delivery is delayed by one millisecond (two steps at dt 0.5 ms).
integration_risks.mitigation: declare the pairing convention; implement delay-matched pairing; validate on a two-neuron hand-computed case
integration_risks.test: hand-computed eligibility and weight change for a known spike pair

integration_risks.risk: Reward derived from the MotorDecoder makes the experiment circular.
integration_risks.evidence: the decoder is deterministic and its thresholds were fixed in Phase 4F; rewarding its output would optimize the measurement.
integration_risks.mitigation: primary reward comes from an external synthetic task outcome; decoder metrics are reported as diagnostics only
integration_risks.test: reward stream does not import or call MotorDecoder; code review and an import-guard test

integration_risks.risk: Credit assignment crosses the cut boundary of the candidate subgraph.
integration_risks.evidence: Phase 4H selects a 64-neuron candidate subgraph; incoming edges at the boundary are absent.
integration_risks.mitigation: plasticity applies only to internal edges; report the number of plastic edges and the fraction of the full graph; do not extrapolate to the whole connectome
integration_risks.test: edge count and endpoint bounds asserted against the candidate graph

integration_risks.risk: Reward magnitude and learning rate interact with pA-scale weights and cause runaway or negligible change.
integration_risks.evidence: weights are pA currents; the rheobase is 150 pA and the cap is 300 pA.
integration_risks.mitigation: declare eta, delta clip and relative bounds a priori; report drift and saturation; abort on a declared firing-rate ceiling
integration_risks.test: bounds and clip tests; saturation diagnostic on the full graph

integration_risks.evidence: no train/eval split exists anywhere in the repository.
integration_risks.mitigation: disjoint seed pools fixed before running; evaluation uses only frozen weights; no parameter selection on evaluation results
integration_risks.test: seed-set intersection is empty; evaluation runs cannot write checkpoints

integration_risks.risk: Learned weights are mistaken for measured connectivity.
integration_risks.evidence: structural counts and transformed weights already coexist in one policy object.
integration_risks.mitigation: separate files and fields; every artifact embeds a model-output label and provenance digests; never modify the connectome artifacts
integration_risks.test: artifact schema requires the label; graph SHA-256 unchanged

integration_risks.risk: Phase 4H artifacts or the root README.md are modified.
integration_risks.evidence: the 4H baseline protects 37 files including README.md.
integration_risks.mitigation: new output directories and a new Phase 5 baseline; no edits to reports/PHASE_4H* or README.md
integration_risks.test: Phase 4H integrity_snapshot reports 37/37 and git diff shows no change to those paths

integration_risks.risk: Float reproducibility differs across machines or BLAS builds.
integration_risks.evidence: weights and currents are float32; reductions such as bincount accumulate in a fixed order but BLAS-backed operations may not.
integration_risks.mitigation: avoid BLAS for per-edge updates; use the same NumPy version; record digests rather than claiming cross-platform identity
integration_risks.test: repeat-run digests on the same machine; documented platform caveat

open_questions: What state representation and value-update rule should the 5B reward predictor use? It must be configurable, documented and separate from plasticity.
What reward delay, magnitude and schedule should the 5B runner exercise? They must be declared before the run.
Which eligibility pairing convention should be primary: same-step or delay-matched? This audit recommends delay-matched and requires a hand-computed test in 5C.
Should traces be stored densely with lazy decay or as a sparse active-edge structure? Decide by measurement in 5C, not by assumption.
Should the plastic simulator in 5D duplicate the loop (recommended here) or add an optional hook to BancSimulator? Duplication is chosen to avoid touching a validated core.
What controlled task and held-out metric will 5E use? It must be independent of the MotorDecoder and specified before any run.

What are the declared values of eta, tau_e, gamma, weight bounds, decay, normalization and delta clip? They must be fixed in configs/plasticity.yaml before 5E-5F and must not be tuned on evaluation results.
Which of the 5E conditions A-G can be implemented fairly, and which must be documented as excluded?
